description_full: Digi International Inc. provides business and mission-critical Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity products, services, and solutions in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and internationally. It operates through IoT Products & Services, and IoT Solutions segments. The company offers cellular routers for mission-critical wireless connectivity; cellular modules to embed cellular communications abilities into the products to deploy and manage intelligent and secure cellular connected products; console servers to provide secure and remote access to network equipment in data centers and at edge locations; and radio frequency products, including embedded wireless modules, off-the-shelf gateways, modems, and adapters under the Digi XBee brand. It also provides embedded system products under the Digi Connect, and ConnectCore brands; and infrastructure management products comprising serial servers, which offers serial port-to-Ethernet integration of devices into wired Ethernet networks; and universal serial bus solutions. In addition, it provides Digi Remote Manager and Lighthouse, a recurring revenue cloud-based service that offers a secure environment for customers to manage connected network devices; SmartSense by Digi for monitoring wirelessly the temperature of food and other perishable or sensitive goods, monitoring facilities or pharmacies by tracking the completion of operating tasks by employees, and quality control and incident management in food service, healthcare, and transportation/logistics industries; and Ventus for MNaaS solutions. Further, the company provides professional services, such as site planning, implementation management, application development, and customer training; data plan subscriptions; and enhanced technical support services, as well as Digi Wireless Design Services. Digi International Inc. was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in Hopkins, Minnesota.

financial_summary: Digi International Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $2.1B market cap on $535M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 52% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $150M in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.85× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.9×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.6%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 3.1% of the shares.

sect: Its 15% operating margin runs 8pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.64x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+25.4% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 536 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 88% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 28% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 36% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 47% and a beta of 1.12, it moves roughly with the market.
About $26.8M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.6x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 64% in the 2020 crash, 27% in the 2022 bear market and 54% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $55.46 (margin of safety -1%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 41%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $27.28 to $116 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on P/FCF 14.2 vs 24.5, richer on P/E 40.4 vs 25.8 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 33% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 7.1% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 5 covering analysts target $79.60 on average, 43% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 7% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.9%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.56).
It runs a 52% gross margin and converts 28% of revenue into free cash flow, or 25% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 2.85x.
ROE of 8% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.4x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 7pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 14.6% of revenue on R&D and 3.4% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.3x net debt to EBITDA ($29.5M of cash against $67.2M of debt), with interest covered 10.9x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.3, in the safe zone).
Goodwill makes up 42% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.4% over 3 years, 11.6% over 5 years and 10.2% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 22.0% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.08 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 46% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 44%.
Capex runs only 0.1x depreciation (0.6% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 36, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.1%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (9 sales, net $8.9M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.6% (0.6% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 2.0% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 947 employees, each generates about $565K of revenue, 1.5x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 6.6% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $158K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.5M (3x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
